title: Configure and verify Layer 2 discovery protocols

questions.question: Which protocol is an IEEE standard that collects information from neighboring devices on their identity and capabilities?
questions.explanation: LLDP is IEEE 802.1AB and provides standards-based neighbor discovery.

correct.explanation: LLDP is IEEE 802.1AB and provides standards-based neighbor discovery.

incorrect.explanation: CDP is Cisco proprietary — the stem asks for an IEEE standard protocol for neighbor identity and capabilities, which is LLDP (802.1AB), not CDP.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Picking Cisco-only CDP for IEEE standard requirement
incorrect.whatItDoes: CDP describes a mechanism that could sound plausible for LLDP is IEEE 802.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Given LLDP is IEEE 802, LLDP matches the tested behavior — CDP applies a different mechanism.

incorrect.explanation: 802.1b is not the IEEE neighbor discovery standard — LLDP is defined in IEEE 802.1AB for collecting neighbor device information.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Selecting nonexistent 802.1b as discovery standard
incorrect.whatItDoes: 802.1b describes a mechanism that could sound plausible for LLDP is IEEE 802.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Given LLDP is IEEE 802, LLDP matches the tested behavior — 802.1b applies a different mechanism.

incorrect.explanation: 802.1a is not LLDP — IEEE 802.1AB defines Link Layer Discovery Protocol for standards-based neighbor information exchange.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Confusing 802.1a with 802.1AB LLDP standard
incorrect.whatItDoes: 802.1a describes a mechanism that could sound plausible for LLDP is IEEE 802.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Given LLDP is IEEE 802, LLDP matches the tested behavior — 802.1a applies a different mechanism.

answerReview.examTip: IEEE neighbor discovery standard → LLDP (802.1AB), not Cisco CDP.

questions.question: You want to turn off CDP on a switch. Which command would you enter?
questions.explanation: no cdp run disables CDP globally.

correct.explanation: no cdp run disables CDP globally.

incorrect.explanation: cdp disable is not valid IOS syntax — the global command to turn off CDP on the entire switch is no cdp run in global configuration mode.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Using invalid cdp disable global command
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config)#cdp disable describes a mechanism that could sound plausible for no cdp run disables CDP globally.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Given no cdp run disables CDP globally, Switch(config-if)#no cdp run matches the tested behavior — Switch(config)#cdp disable applies a different mechanism.

incorrect.explanation: no cdp enable under an interface disables CDP on that port only — the stem asks to turn off CDP on the whole switch, which requires global no cdp run.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Using per-interface disable for global CDP off
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config-if)#no cdp enable describes a mechanism that could sound plausible for no cdp run disables CDP globally.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Given no cdp run disables CDP globally, Switch(config-if)#no cdp run matches the tested behavior — Switch(config-if)#no cdp enable applies a different mechanism.

incorrect.explanation: no cdp alone is incomplete IOS syntax — the recognized global command is no cdp run to disable CDP switch-wide.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Using incomplete no cdp without run keyword
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config)#no cdp describes a mechanism that could sound plausible for no cdp run disables CDP globally.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Given no cdp run disables CDP globally, Switch(config-if)#no cdp run matches the tested behavior — Switch(config)#no cdp applies a different mechanism.

answerReview.examTip: Disable CDP globally → no cdp run. Per-port → no cdp enable on interface.

questions.question: How often are CDP frames sent out of the device by default?
questions.explanation: CDP advertises every 60 seconds by default.

correct.explanation: CDP advertises every 60 seconds by default.

incorrect.explanation: CDP default timer is 60 seconds, not 30 — advertisements are sent once per minute unless changed with cdp timer.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Confusing 30-second interval with CDP default
incorrect.whatItDoes: Every 30 seconds describes a mechanism that could sound plausible for CDP advertises every 60 seconds by default.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Given CDP advertises every 60 seconds by default, Every 60 seconds matches the tested behavior — Every 30 seconds applies a different mechanism.

incorrect.explanation: 90 seconds is not the default CDP advertisement interval — IOS sends CDP updates every 60 seconds by default.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Selecting 90 seconds as CDP timer default
incorrect.whatItDoes: Every 90 seconds describes a mechanism that could sound plausible for CDP advertises every 60 seconds by default.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Given CDP advertises every 60 seconds by default, Every 60 seconds matches the tested behavior — Every 90 seconds applies a different mechanism.

incorrect.explanation: 180 seconds is the default CDP hold-time, not the advertisement interval — frames are sent every 60 seconds, and neighbors are held for 180 seconds of silence.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Confusing CDP hold-time (180 s) with timer (60 s)
incorrect.whatItDoes: Every 180 seconds describes a mechanism that could sound plausible for CDP advertises every 60 seconds by default.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Given CDP advertises every 60 seconds by default, Every 60 seconds matches the tested behavior — Every 180 seconds applies a different mechanism.

answerReview.examTip: CDP defaults: timer 60 s, hold-time 180 s — do not swap them.

questions.question: What is the default value of the CDP holddown timer for CDP entries?

incorrect.explanation: 30 seconds is not the default CDP hold-time — IOS keeps neighbor entries for 180 seconds without updates before removing them.

questions.question: You have several non-Cisco IP phones and you want to allow automatic power adjustments on the Cisco Power over an Ethernet (PoE) switch. Which command will allow you to achieve this?

incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch(config)#lldp enable describes a mechanism that could sound plausible for lldp run enables LLDP globally, including LLDP-MED capabilities.

incorrect.whyWrongHere: Given lldp run enables LLDP globally, including LLDP-MED capabilities, Switch(config)#lldp run matches the tested behavior — Switch#lldp enable applies a different mechanism.

questions.question:
CDP neighbor detail (SwitchB):
Device ID: SwitchB
Entry address(es): IP 192.168.1.2
Platform: cisco WS-C2960, Capabilities: Switch
Interface: GigabitEthernet0/2, Port ID (outgoing port): GigabitEthernet0/1
Holdtime: 162 sec

The following output shows the output of the CDP details. Which statement is correct about what is displayed?
choices: The advertisement was seen 162 seconds ago.
Switch B interface Gi0/1 connects to Switch A.
Switch B interface Gi0/2 connects to Switch A.
The IP address of Switch B is 192.168.1.1.
questions.explanation: CDP detail output identifies the local and remote interfaces, holdtime, and management address.

correct.explanation: The Interface field shows the local port receiving CDP (Gi0/2 on this switch) — it connects to the neighbor's Port ID (Gi0/1 on SwitchB).

incorrect.explanation: Holdtime (162 sec) is time remaining before the entry ages — not when the last advertisement was seen.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Reading holdtime as last-seen timestamp
incorrect.whatItDoes: The advertisement was seen 162 seconds ago. describes a mechanism that could sound plausible for neighbor.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Given neighbor, Switch B interface Gi0/2 connects to Switch A. matches the tested behavior — The advertisement was seen 162 seconds ago. applies a different mechanism.

incorrect.explanation: Port ID lists the neighbor's outgoing interface (Gi0/1 on SwitchB) — the local Interface field is Gi0/2 facing SwitchB.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Swapping local Interface with neighbor Port ID
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch B interface Gi0/1 connects to Switch A. describes a mechanism that could sound plausible for neighbor.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Given neighbor, Switch B interface Gi0/2 connects to Switch A. matches the tested behavior — Switch B interface Gi0/1 connects to Switch A. applies a different mechanism.

incorrect.explanation: Entry address shows SwitchB management IP 192.168.1.2 — 192.168.1.1 is not listed in this CDP detail output.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Inventing neighbor IP not shown in CDP output
incorrect.whatItDoes: The IP address of Switch B is 192.168.1.1. shifts the answer to IP/Layer 3 addressing instead of Ethernet MAC learning.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Given neighbor, Switch B interface Gi0/2 connects to Switch A. matches the tested behavior — The IP address of Switch B is 192.168.1.1. applies a different mechanism.

answerReview.examTip: CDP detail: Interface = local port; Port ID = neighbor's port facing you.
